content:
Indian marketing taught me to be loud. German marketing taught me that silence can sell.

In India, the best content is abundant. 

Colour, emotion, celebration, community. 

Festivals are marketing events. 
Family is a recurring character. 
Warmth is the default setting.

In Germany, the best content is precise. 

Less noise, more trust. 

The audience doesn't need to be charmed, they need to be convinced. 
Credibility over charisma.

When I moved from one market to the other, my first instinct was to keep doing what had worked.

It didn't work.

Not because my skills were wrong. But because I was speaking my language to an audience with a completely different one.

The shift I had to make: stop translating your content. Start thinking in the audience's culture.

That's the difference between a marketer who can execute and one who can actually connect.

The most powerful thing about working across cultures isn't the perspective you gain. It's the assumptions you lose.
comment: A useful shift is recognizing that culture shapes not just messaging style, but the buyer's definition of evidence. What builds trust in one market can create friction in another.
